scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

The person is a 33-year-old man living with his parents. He pays $200 rent, which is market rate where they live. He's been living there for a long time and generally avoids his parents, locking himself in his room. Recently, there was a bathroom flood, so they're remodeling his section, leading to more interactions. 

Today, his parents went to Costco and when they got home, he was playing Apex on the couch. His mom asked him to help bring in groceries, and he said he'd do it in a minute. He was too into the game to notice they were making multiple trips. His dad then told him to get up, and when he still said in a minute, his dad grabbed the controller and it turned into a shouting match. Now, the parents are checking into a hotel and expecting him to find a place by Friday, which seems impossible. They also brought up his younger brother, who is married with kids and got promoted, implying he's the golden child.

The person is asking if he's the asshole for not helping with the groceries, considering he pays rent and feels he has the right to say no to such requests.

Alright, so the main issue here is whether it's morally acceptable for him to refuse to help his parents with bringing in groceries, especially after they asked multiple times and it led to a shouting match.

First, I need to consider the context. He's an adult paying rent, which is market rate. So, he's contributing financially. However, he's still living with his parents, which might be seen as a choice, but he's comfortable with it because it's cheap and meets his needs.

When his parents asked him to help, he was playing a game and didn't respond immediately. They had to make several trips, and his dad eventually took the controller, leading to an argument. Now, the parents are leaving and expecting him to find a place quickly, which seems stressful.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for him to refuse to help, given that he pays rent?

I think the key points here are responsibility, respect, and consideration for others. Even though he's paying rent, he's still living under their roof, and they're his parents. There's an expectation of mutual respect and helping out, especially when they're doing something for the household, like bringing in groceries.

He might feel that paying rent gives him the right to say no, but in many cultures and family dynamics, living with parents often comes with certain responsibilities, even if you're paying rent. It's not just about the money; it's also about being part of a family unit.

His refusal to help, especially after being asked multiple times, could be seen as disrespectful. It's one thing to say you'll help in a minute, but if you're too engrossed in a game to notice their efforts, it might come off as inconsiderate.

The shouting match escalated the situation, leading to the parents leaving. That's a significant consequence. It's possible that his initial refusal contributed to the conflict, making the situation worse.

On the other hand, he might feel that he's an adult and should have the autonomy to choose how to spend his time. However, living with others, especially family, often requires compromise and consideration of their needs and feelings.

So, considering all this, I think his action of refusing to help, especially after being asked multiple times, is morally unacceptable. It shows a lack of respect and consideration for his parents, even though he's contributing financially. The refusal led to a conflict that resulted in them leaving, which is a serious outcome.
